Latent values for Lender Spreads, Chip Lead Times and Bitcoin Hashprice are mapped from this scenario's own market path (public quantities); Revenue Gap, Grid Reserve Margin and Efficiency Index are authored. Displayed values add observation noise; the sharp range brackets the latent value.
DO_NOT_EXPOSE: authoring_latent must never be read by bots, the UI, or 'Read the market'. Runtime reads only series[].displayed, .arrow and .sharp.
neutral_tolerance: +-12 (structural drift: halving, efficiency trend, grid retirements)

trigger.title: Open-Weights Week
trigger.narrative: In October 2027 an open-weights model matches frontier quality on the benchmarks that matter and can be served at about a tenth of the cost per token. Chip stocks fall double digits in a day and token prices collapse 8-10x. AI-lab tenants invoke 'material change' reopeners on contracts priced for scarce compute; hyperscalers hold their leases but tell you next year's orders will be trimmed. After four to six quarters, cheaper tokens unlock new uses and demand rebounds (the Jevons effect), mostly for newer chip generations and inference-optimised sites; older Hopper capacity never fully recovers.

decoy.reason: A record summer heat wave and two delayed plant retirements squeeze reserve margins in PJM and ERCOT. It is weather and supply, not AI load growth; hyperscaler load additions are actually flat that year.
decoy.tell: Reserve margins tighten with no matching rise in lead times, no narrowing of the Revenue Gap and no rise in spot rents. Capacity prices spike for two quarters, then ease.
decoy.fair_in_hindsight: A tight grid is exactly what Lift-Off looks like, and the capacity-price spike was real. But nothing else in the panel confirmed a demand boom, and the Efficiency Index was already climbing.
